title: Multi Agent Rl
motto: Single-agent RL assumes the environment is stationary. Put two learning agents in the same world and that assumption breaks: each agent is part of the other's environment, and both are changing. Multi-agent RL is the set of tricks to make learning converge when the Markov assumption no longer holds.

steps.title: Core idea
steps.body: Single-agent RL assumes the environment is stationary. Put two learning agents in the same world and that assumption breaks: each agent is part of the other's environment, and both are changing. Multi-agent RL is the set of tricks to make learning converge when the Markov assumption no longer holds.

steps.title: Why this matters
cards: A robot learning to navigate a room is a single-agent RL problem. A soccer team is not. AlphaStar vs StarCraft opponents is not. A marketplace of bidding agents is not. Two cars negotiating a four-way stop is not. Many-on-many real-world problems are not.

In every multi-agent setting, from the perspective of any one agent, the other agents *are* part of the environment. As they learn and change their behavior, the environment becomes non-stationary. The Markov property — "next state depends only on current state and my action" — gets violated because the next state also depends on what the *other* agents chose, and their policies are moving targets.
